gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Almendra Display brings an ornate, bookish flourish with a tall x-height and curves that never pinch shut. Noto Sans Syriac Western sits beneath it, sans-serif and tidy.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-syriac-easter: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern has tall, friendly lowercase and curve endings that stay well apart, while Audiowide stamps out tiled, pipe-bent letters above it. Make that heading small and its wide gaps would start to look sparse.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Menacing and jagged, Eater keeps its ascenders short. Eater is best at snarling up top with a gentle thick-to-thin shift, while Noto Sans Tagalog does its best work as a quiet sans, its middle zone dominating each line.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Stubby, playful and loud, Flavors draws diagonals as hefty as its stems under a towering x-height. Noto Sans Tagbanwa backs it up in a modern sans, its open curves giving the heading room.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-tai-th: Noto Sans Tai Tham reads crowded toward the top, its c wide open to the eye. Almendra Display adds the literary ornament, and that gap between ornate and sans-serif is the pair's best trait.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads smooth, with strokes that taper out before touching and little step up to capitals. Audiowide, by contrast, is all hairline-free tiles, so a small heading would lose its futuristic punch.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri reads polished and modern, with high-waisted lowercase and small round letters left generously unclosed beneath the heading. Flavors, whose round bowls keep a uniform wall, makes the strongest single contrast: whimsy against sans-serif restraint.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-tamil-: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement reads stocky and contemporary, its round forms like open parentheses inside a very tall middle band. Almendra Display handles ornate, literary headings best, while the plain sans carries the text.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified even at ordinary size, with terminals that stop far from the stem. Audiowide excels at monoline, futuristic headings, and the sans body does its best work as modern running text.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Aggressive and dark, Eater leans on heavier verticals, like a gently tilted nib, with wide gaps between letters. Noto Sans Tangsa follows in a sans-serif with inviting round openings, so long paragraphs would feel approachable.
